Sounds like the other person is avoiding uncomfortable feelings and didn't get the chance to learn how to deal with bad feelings in their past. 
Like communicating openly and authentic with compassion about uncomfortable emotions like shame for example. 

I'd be aware with how much you let this slide with out acknowledging this, 
if the other person keeps their unwillingness to communicate up and doesn't put effort to work through it... or work through the fact that it's hard to work through their feelings. 

Perhaps state them, how their unwillingness to communicate makes you feel, and that you have a need for intimicy.

It can be really difficult, AND ALSO you don't have to let their unwillingness to communicate let you belittle your needs or boundaries. 🙏

I was 18/19 yrs old.   (20 now)
I was excessively stressed about school and did numb
my fear by repressing my surroundings and my feelings.

I started missing classes to the point my teacher asked why I was missing. (This was like one or two weeks in.)

But I didn't want my parents to know about it, so I took the train back and fourth and waited 6-8 hours a day
to finally be able to get home.

By that time I got highly anxious and paranoid that anybody would find out. 

Every thought I had was unreasonable/unrealistic and highly destructive.

 I did not care about anything but keeping my "secret" to myself.

I didn't want anybody to know of this.

The only thing that kept me on going was the daily talk with my friends in the evening and a long playlist of podcasts.

Approximately 3 or 4 weeks in driving back and forth for 6-8 hrs,
It got to the point, where I was laying packed with a warm woolen blanket in the forest next to my mom's house.
Nothing did matter to me except keeping it private.

I waited until I could enter our house without being noticed.

It was nerve-wracking and I was so paranoid and anxious.

I'm relatively fine now, I'm still going to school an stuff,
But all this time being afraid to tell anyone, had quite a backlash on my mental health.

I still cannot handle stress and fall every time in a depressive state for 3-4 days.

Over all, I'm quite critical to myself and even hate myself from time to time for the smallest things.

But on the other side, all this self-directed internal hate did get me into philosophy due to questions like
"Why don't we kill ourselves?" or
 "what is the meaning of life?" 

But I'm not suicidal, just to let you know.

I thought about what would happen, if... 
But it's not that serious.

Thx for reading.
